analysis.title: Global Markets Vol Weekly - 3rd November 2026
key_insights: October saw the largest cross-asset correlation shift since the start of the Iran war. US bonds went from selling off with risk to rallying when risk sells off, and SPX/bond correlation moved from +50% to -50% over the month.
US rates correlation to SPX, gold and oil all flipped sign in October. The dollar's correlation to SPX also flipped from negative (SPX down, dollar up) to positive (SPX down, dollar down).
Average cross-asset 20d realized correlation is at its lowest level in years. Only non-AI stocks vs bonds and bonds vs some G10 FX (mainly yen, somewhat EUR) saw correlations rise.
Implied SPX/Rates and SPX/USDJPY correlation have not repriced and remain near levels from a month ago, which UBS sees as an opportunity to buy risk-off hybrid hedges (Dual Digitals).
Event pricing for the US midterms (Wed Nov 4) faded to a 70bps SPX implied move at Thursday's close, then rebounded to 1.04% at Monday's close, 8bps ahead of the move priced for Friday's NFP.

The largest SPX move priced for the rest of the week is one-third of Friday's 2.5% max drawdown and one-half of Monday's high-low decline, so UBS sees front-end options as good value for investors reluctant to take outright exposure.
Event weights on some FX vol curves rebounded (EURUSD implied move 39bps) and rates curves carry a bit more premium (TLT implied move about 1%).
US leveraged ETFs took in $28bn over the last five months, concentrated in recent weeks. SOXL drove $16bn of that, with buying concentrated on down days including Friday.
Rebalance flows on Friday Oct 30 required leveraged funds to sell $36bn in total, including $16.5bn of semis. UBS ranks it the 3rd largest in history, behind only a June 2026 session.
Friday Oct 30 fund inflows included SPY $5.19bn, QQQ $4.01bn, SOXX $1.06bn and SOXL $1.90bn (2nd on a 3-year rank). SOXL volume was concentrated in the last two hours.

Options investors kept trading counter-trend on Friday: ten of thirteen half-hour windows saw delta bought on down moves or sold on up moves. Support faded late in the session, with $6.6bn of delta buying on the 10:00-10:30 decline but modest selling on the 13:30-14:30 decline.

Friday Oct 30 was one of the busiest 0DTE sessions ever, with $3.5tn of SPX notional (4th all-time). Options activity skewed to the buy side, leaving market makers short gamma on Friday and Monday Nov 2.

Offshore China equities rebounded, with HSCEI and FXI up about 3% from the Oct 22 lows, led by financials (SOE banks) rather than internet as in July's rally. The CSI Banks index hit a YTD high at month-end.
FXI 1-month ATMF implied vol sits near the 14th percentile of its 3.5-year range, which UBS cites as support for tactical upside via calls.

UBS Research argues the market overprices the AI bill and gives limited credit to cash-flow recovery or AI monetization, so a less negative earnings outlook for China internet could broaden the rebound.
Gold is down 17% since late August. Its most persistent correlation has been the inverse relationship with the USD, and recent USD strength is attributed to US energy and AI exceptionalism.
Gold closing below $4017 on Oct 23 met Jason Perl's minimum targets for completing the correction from $5600. 3m implied vols for GLD show puts bid over calls even with spot below $3900.

The cross-asset hedging screen shows hedge payoff convexity at low levels across most equities after recent vol mini-spikes, with SMI puts and US index puts the exceptions. UBS favors spread structures. USDCNH calls, GDX and GLD upside still screen well, and TLT calls may offer value, though calls now trade over puts.

sector_views.rationale: Rotation to defensives led the offshore rebound, with SOE banks leading. UBS sees continued defensive support as potential upside for FXI and HSCEI.
Dip buying in SOXL and late-session semis buying met large mechanical rebalance selling of $16.5bn on Oct 30.

earnings_insights: Expectations for China internet earnings are described as low, with soft domestic consumption and AI investment concerns weighing on the sector. UBS Research argues a less negative outlook could broaden the rebound.

vol_and_positioning: SPX implied one-day move for Wed Nov 4 is 1.04% as of Mon Nov 2 close, down from a 70bps low on Thursday's close.
Largest SPX move priced through the rest of the week is about one-third of Friday's 2.5% max drawdown.

Leveraged fund rebalance on Oct 30 required $36bn of selling, the 3rd largest on record, including semis -$16.5bn, NDX -$9.7bn, single stock -$3.2bn and SPX -$2.1bn.
SPX 0DTE traded $3.5tn notional on Oct 30 (4th all-time), with market makers short gamma on Oct 30 and Nov 2.
Options investors trade counter-trend, buying delta on dips and selling on rallies.

Brent 2M ATM implied vol is 51.0 with USO at 54.5, both at high 5-year percentiles (89% and 93%).
geopolitical: Iran war and the resulting energy shock shaped cross-asset correlations in prior months, and a possible Iran resolution is cited as a driver that could weaken the dollar.
US midterm elections on Wednesday Nov 4 are priced as a vol event.
A Middle East breakthrough is cited as a possible catalyst for a rebound, and Middle East progress reversing as a possible driver of an extended drawdown.

tension_points.bull_case: A rebound into the end of the week is possible on a midterm wall of worry or a Middle East breakthrough, and the 7580 call makes 3.1x back at Thursday's close.
tension_points.bear_case: An extended drawdown is possible if Middle East progress reverses or NFP surprises, as realized moves have exceeded implied (Friday max drawdown 2.5%).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Largest SPX move priced through the rest of the week is only about one-third of Friday's 2.5% max drawdown, so options look cheap for either direction.

tension_points.bull_case: Gold met Jason Perl's minimum targets for completing the correction from $5600, and UBS sees modest upside over the next few months.
tension_points.bear_case: A strong USD has driven the 17% decline, and puts remain bid over calls.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further dollar rally, since the gold/USD inverse correlation is the most persistent driver.
